f1.quote: Heating proceeded at 10 °C/min in 50 °C increments, with a 5 min hold at each setpoint and XRD scans over 2θ=30–80°.

f2.quote: air produced a thick duplex scale and a pronounced Al-depleted, FCC/B2-denuded subsurface zone, whereas vacuum produced a much thinner scale and thin transformed subsurface layer.

f3.quote: Heating proceeded at 10 °C/min in 50 °C increments, with a 5 min hold at each setpoint and XRD scans over 2θ=30–80°.

f4.quote: The vacuum was reported as approximately 4.2×10^-6 atm overall pressure, with another section estimating p(O2)=8.82×10^-7 atm; oxygen partial pressure was not measured directly.

f5.quote: Heating transformed the initial BCC/B2 substrate through FCC and Cr-Fe-rich sigma-phase formation at intermediate temperatures, followed by sigma dissolution at higher temperature.

f6.quote: Selective oxidation occurred primarily by outward diffusion of Al, and secondarily Cr, to react with oxygen.

f7.quote: Oxidation generated an Al-rich external Al2O3 scale with a Cr-rich/Cr2O3 inner region

f8.quote: High oxygen availability accelerated scale growth and Al consumption, producing external Al2O3 over an inner Cr2O3-rich layer and driving Al depletion and phase transformation beneath the scale. Under low p(O2), slower oxidation kinetics limited scale growth.

f9.quote: Relative to the initial BCC/B2 alloy and to low-p(O2) exposure, heating in air was expected to produce earlier/more extensive oxidation, a thicker Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale, and stronger Al-depletion-induced subsurface transformation; vacuum exposure was expected to retain only a thin, predominantly alumina

f12.quote: vacuum exposure was expected to retain only a thin, predominantly alumina protective film.
